int xchg(int *addr, int newval) {

      
    int result;

      
    asm volatile("lock xchg %0, %1"

      
        : "+m"(*addr), "=a"(result) : "1"(newval) : "cc");

      
    return result;

      
}

SpinCompare-and-swap: check and set at once

    

      
void spin_lock(lock_t *lk) {

      
retry:

      
    if (cmpxchg(&lk->status, UNLOCKED, LOCKED) != UNLOCKED) {

      
        goto retry;

      
    }

      
}

      
void spin_unlock(lock_t *lk) {

      
    lk->status = UNLOCKED;

      
    __sync_synchronize();

      
}

Pitfallsl or I? One typo, no lock

    

      
T1: lock(&l); sum++; unlock(&l);

      
T2: lock(&I); sum++; unlock(&I);

    

    

      
int withdraw(int n) {

      
    lock(&lk);

      
    if (balance < n) return -1;   // unlock?

      
    balance -= n;

      
    unlock(&lk);

      
    return 0;

      
}

CostOne core works, the others watch

    

      
#define T      4          // four threads

      
#define ROUNDS 2000       // each enters 2,000 times

      
#define WORK   100000     // and stays for 100,000 sum++

      
void *worker(void *arg) {

      
    for (int r = 0; r < ROUNDS; r++) {

      
        lock();                  // spin, or mutex

      
        for (int i = 0; i < WORK; i++) sum++;

      
        unlock();

      
    }

      
}

CostLinux 2008: take a ticket

    
Take a numberfirst come, first served

    

      
typedef struct { int ticket; int turn; } lock_t;

      
void lock(lock_t *lock) {

      
    int myturn = FetchAndAdd(&lock->ticket);

      
    while (lock->turn != myturn)

      
        ; // spin

      
}

      
void unlock(lock_t *lock) {

      
    lock->turn = lock->turn + 1;

      
}

Kernelxv6: interrupts off, then spin

    

      
void acquire(struct spinlock *lk) {

      
  pushcli(); // disable interrupts to avoid deadlock.

      
  if(holding(lk))

      
    panic("acquire");

      
  while(xchg(&lk->locked, 1) != 0)

      
    ;

      
  __sync_synchronize();

      
  lk->cpu = mycpu();

      
}

      
void release(struct spinlock *lk) {

      
  if(!holding(lk))

      
    panic("release");

      
  lk->cpu = 0;

      
  __sync_synchronize();

      
  asm volatile("movl $0, %0" : "+m" (lk->locked) : );

      
  popcli();

      
}

MutexA system call costs 130 lock addq

    

      
const int N = 10000000;

      
t0 = now_ns();

      
for (int i = 0; i < N; i++)

      
    asm volatile("lock addq $1, %0" : "+m"(x));  // user space only

      
t1 = now_ns();

      
for (int i = 0; i < N; i++)

      
    syscall(SYS_getppid);                  // into the kernel and back

      
t2 = now_ns();

      
printf("lock addq:       %6.2f ns\n", (double)(t1 - t0) / N);

      
printf("getppid syscall: %6.2f ns\n", (double)(t2 - t1) / N);

      lock is freelock is taken
      spinone xchg: fastspins: burns a CPU

KERNEL

    
wait queue for &val

    
futex_wait(&val, v): sleep, if val is still v
futex_wake(&val, n): wake up to n sleepers

    
No contention, no system call: enter the kernel only to wait or wake

    
futex_wait / futex_wake as defined in Drepper, "Futexes Are Tricky" (v1.6, 2011), appendix · schematic

  

  

    

    
FutexDrepper's futex mutex, step by step

    

      
void lock() {

      
    int c;

      
    if ((c = cmpxchg(val, 0, 1)) != 0) {

      
        if (c != 2)

      
            c = xchg(val, 2);

      
        while (c != 0) {

      
            futex_wait(&val, 2);

      
            c = xchg(val, 2);

      
        }

      
    }

      
}

      
void unlock() {

      
    if (atomic_dec(val) != 1) {

      
        val = 0;

      
        futex_wake(&val, 1);

      
    }

      
}

FutexFutexes are tricky

    

    
Drepper, on the inventors' own code"… as of this writing the code is actually incorrect. This exemplifies that using futexes is really tricky since they provide problems even to their inventors."

    
A bug inside glibc's thread library"This bug was present in some form for many months in the NPTL implementation." Fixing it sped up one real application 8 to 10 times on a four-processor machine.

    
Do not write your own futex lock: on Linux, pthread_mutex already does it

    
Ulrich Drepper, "Futexes Are Tricky", Red Hat, v1.6 (5 Nov 2011; first draft 12 Oct 2003), preface and §4 · Franke, Russell, Kirkwood, "Fuss, Futexes and Furwocks", Ottawa Linux Symposium 2002 · "man 7 futex | claude Explain": from the source lecture

MeasureA syscall in every lock: 40× slower

    

      
static _Atomic int klock = 0;   /* 0 = unlocked, 1 = locked */

      
void lock_force_kernel(void) {

      
  for (;;) {

      
    int expected = 0;

      
    if (atomic_compare_exchange_weak_explicit(&klock, &expected, 1, ...)) {

      
      futex_wait_int((int*)&klock, 2);  /* returns at once, but it trapped */

      
      return;

      
    }

      
    futex_wait_int((int*)&klock, 1);    /* contended: sleep in the kernel */

      
  }

      
}

      
void unlock_force_kernel(void) {

      
  atomic_store_explicit(&klock, 0, memory_order_release);

      
  futex_wake_int((int*)&klock, 1);      /* traps even if nobody waits */

      
}

    

    

    
trap: 577 ns with 1 thread → 737, 839, 1000, 1056 ns with 2, 4, 8, 1640 × the spin lock and 23 × the mutex at 1 thread; the mutex makes no syscall when the lock is free

    
pthread_mutex is fast because it skips the kernel when the lock is free

TakeawaysWho waits, and how

    
    
spin lockone xchg; waiters burn CPUs and bounce the line

    
kernel spininterrupts off, very short sections

    
mutexwaiters sleep; about 1 µs per syscall

    
futexuser space when free, kernel only to wait

    
measureevery T, 5 runs, real ns

    
Use one big lock first · the holder must be able to run (Pathfinder) · tickets make spinning fair
